title: Damage settlements with shelter hotels
question: After the shelter programme ended, what did the City pay hotel owners for damage and lost use, and how large was that beside what it had paid for the rooms?
finding: The Board approved 9 settlements with hotel owners for damage by shelter guests and resulting loss of use, $44.5 million in all, between 22 December 2022 and 23 June 2023. The largest is $19.5 million for the Hotel Whitcomb ($42,484 a room). Across the 9 that can be matched to a room agreement the settlements come to 27% of what had been paid for the rooms, from 7.9% to 57%. The analyst had warned of it: under the agreements “the City is responsible for all repair costs associated with restoring the hotel to its previous condition, even if they exceed the contingency amount”, and by July 2022 “at least two hotels, Hotel Union Square and Tilden, have demanded repair costs above the not to exceed contract amounts”.
how: Board files titled as settlements whose text says the claim involves property damage to a named hotel caused by shelter-in-place guests. The hotel is named as the title names it and the claimant as the file names it; each is matched to its room agreement by the hotel’s name (or, through the project’s owner-groups, the owner’s registered names). “Against room payments” is the settlement divided by everything paid on the room agreement. “Seen in the payment file” is what the payment file shows paid to the same payee from the judgments and claims account. The quotations are from the Budget and Legislative Analyst’s reports of 7 September and 13 July 2022.
limits: Each settlement was voted on and each file records a mutual release with both sides bearing their own costs. The agreements made the City responsible for restoring the hotels after up to three years of continuous use, so repair claims at the end were foreseeable and say nothing against the owners. The titles give one figure for damage and lost use together and do not say what an inspection found or what the owner first demanded. Repairs paid during the stay under each agreement’s contingency are inside the room payments, not here. What would settle whether the sums were fair: the condition reports signed at move-in and move-out, the owners’ itemised claims and the City’s own damage estimates. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).

columns.t: Hotel, as the file names it

rows.claimant: Euphoria Hospitality, Inc., dba Nob Hill Hotel
